bugs: config/queue.php:76-83 — the new 'redis-long' connection uses the same Redis queue name ('default') as the standard 'redis' connection, whose retry_after is 90. A plain `queue:work redis` worker can therefore pop SyncSupplierStock with a 90s reservation. Another worker then re-reserves it mid-run, it fails with MaxAttemptsExceeded (Tries 1), and that failure releases the unique lock early. The long connection needs its own queue name.
app/Console/Commands/PruneAbandonedCarts.php:22-23 — the delete runs on whereKey($ids) without re-applying the cutoff. A cart touched between the pluck and the delete still gets deleted (small race).

strengths: Every scheduled task uses onOneServer, the commands also use withoutOverlapping with expiries well under the interval, and the time zone is set to Europe/Copenhagen
Cart prune at 03:30 avoids the DST-ambiguous hour

SyncSupplierStock uses modern queue attributes (Connection, Tries, Timeout, FailOnTimeout, UniqueFor): Timeout 2700 < UniqueFor 3300 < 3600, and retry_after 3000 > Timeout, so a killed worker's lock expires before the next hourly tick
Scopes take an explicit cutoff, which keeps them easy to test

Tests cover the report's exact UTC firing time in winter and summer, re-queueing after the lock expires (a killed worker), the invariant between timeout, lock and retry_after, the target connection, mail rendering, a multi-batch prune with an output count, and the missing-config failure path
Pruning by batched id pluck + delete stays memory-safe and uses the updated_at index

v.rationale: The two implementations are nearly the same design. Both use onOneServer and bounded withoutOverlapping, schedule in Europe/Copenhagen time, and ship a ShouldBeUnique job with modern queue attributes on a separate 'redis-long' connection. Both have the same real flaw: 'redis-long' reuses the 'default' queue name, so a standard redis worker (retry_after 90) can pick up the 40-minute job. That re-reserves the job mid-run and releases its unique lock early. impl-2 makes this more likely to bite because it sets QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis. My probes showed both handle DST correctly (prune fires once on the spring-forward day and once on the fall-back day, and the report fires at 05:30 UTC in summer), prune memory-safely in about 11-12 queries for 5,000 rows, keep carts exactly 30 days old, and allow re-queueing after the lock expires. impl-2's prune is slightly better (chunkById plus a re-checked scope), and it has a schedule:run integration test. impl-1's tests are clearly stronger, though: they cover DST firing instants, lock expiry after a killed worker, the timeout/lock/retry_after invariant, and the target connection. impl-2 has a vacuous 'dispatched only once while lock held' test that dispatches just once, and it tests no DST dates. That makes impl-1 the better implementation.
